findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains `pass` — it does not implement the abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` that StatefulDetectorHandler declares with @abc.abstractmethod. Previously this class provided a concrete `evaluate()` implementation that satisfied DetectorHandler's single abstract method, so it could be instantiated. After this change, any attempt to instantiate MetricAlertDetectorHandler (e.g. via `Detector.detector_handler` -> `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for a detector of type `metric_alert_fire`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`, crashing any code path that processes a metric alert detector.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still describes a list return value
findings.body: The docstring for StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate() says "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the method signature and implementation were changed in this PR to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. The stale docstring is misleading for future readers/maintainers.

findings.title: No test exercises instantiation of MetricAlertDetectorHandler after refactor
findings.body: There is no test verifying that `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` (or any detector configured with the `metric_alert_fire` group type) can actually be constructed via `Detector.detector_handler`. Since the class is now abstract (see related finding), this would fail at runtime, but no test catches this regression.

findings.title: module-level logger is now unused in this file
findings.body: The `logger` defined at module scope (`logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`) was previously used to log a "Duplicate detector state group keys found" error inside `process_detectors`. That logging call was removed as part of switching `evaluate()` to return a dict, and there is no other use of `logger` remaining in this file, leaving dead code that linters would flag.
